source_taxonomy: MAST (Multi-Agent System Failure Taxonomy), Cemri et al. 2025, "Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?" — 14 failure modes across 3 categories, derived by inter-annotator analysis of real multi-agent system traces (independent of this work).
note: Author-assigned thematic association between our 9 scenario families and independently-defined MAST modes. This is a face-valid mapping by the authors, NOT an independent annotation: there is no inter-rater agreement or third-party labeling, so it should be read as 'each family can be manually associated with a MAST category', not as external taxonomy validation. It mitigates (does not eliminate) the circularity concern that families merely rename the gate's checks.

families.rationale: An agent grounds on context belonging to a different concurrent run/history.
A pre-pause constraint that has been superseded is still acted upon.
A retired compliance policy is followed after it was replaced.
State from a sibling branch leaks into the active task scope.
A required upstream artifact is not propagated to the downstream agent.
A record is read by a receiver outside its allowed-reader set.
The critical record is crowded out over a long horizon.
The final decision cannot be justified/verified from the event graph.

A record whose static attributes all match but whose source lies on an abandoned sibling branch (not in the active message's causal ancestry) governs the answer. Distinct from branch_merge: here every visible field is valid and only causal-graph reachability separates it.
